findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add a criterion that exercises the real /rest/api/3/project/search envelope (a recorded/contract fixture matching Jira Cloud's paginated response) or document why offline fixtures suffice for the transport boundary.
evidence: 'fake/injected transport (no live Jira): a fake client whose _direct_rest_get returns a project/search page'
E6(f): a proving command on a mock substitute that bypasses the new behavior does not prove the criterion
findings.finding: The preflight introduces a new live REST boundary (GET /rest/api/3/project/search), but every acceptance criterion is verified only against a fake/injected _direct_rest_get; no criterion exercises the real Cloud transport parsing/pagination end-to-end, and there is no documented rationale/deferral for the absence of a live check.
scenarios: The real project/search envelope shape (values[].key / isLast / nextPage semantics) differs from the fake fixture and the probe silently mis-parses against live Jira
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note that the fake fixture mirrors the documented Jira Cloud project/search envelope, and cite the endpoint contract, or defer a live smoke check to a named follow-up with rationale.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the wiring premise: confirm which signal run_pass_result can read BEFORE reconcile_once to identify dry-run/preview (target_mode / route), and note that reconcile-check is dispatched via _run_reconcile_check (__main__.py:627), not run_pass_result — so either drop reconcile-check from the run_pass_result skip enumeration or specify a second gate at that entrypoint.
evidence: __main__.py:627 dispatches reconcile-check via `_run_reconcile_check(repo_root)`, a distinct path that never calls run_pass_result (grep: run_pass_result( appears only at __main__.py:431 in run_pass and _lib_ops.py:195)

run_pass_result signature (__main__.py:469) takes target_mode and route but no --mode; it calls reconcile.reconcile_once at 506 and only learns no_write from the RESULT (line 524), i.e. after the call

reconcile.py:234 comment: 'target_mode None defaults to LIVE → persists. dry-run / reconcile-check' — the no-write behavior is decided inside reconcile_once, downstream of where the preflight must gate
findings.finding: The plan's wiring claim rests on a partially-false premise: it says to skip 'read-only passes (dry-run / reconcile-check / preview)' at run_pass_result, but reconcile-check never flows through run_pass_result — it is dispatched by the separate _run_reconcile_check(repo_root) at __main__.py:627 (which does not call run_pass_result). Additionally the dry-run no-write verdict is computed inside reconcile_once (reconcile.py:234), so it is not observable BEFORE the reconcile_once call where the preflight must run; run_pass_result's only pre-call read-only signals are target_mode and route, and the plan does not state which it will read.
findings.location: Approach / Sequencing — 'Wire it at the reconcile pass entry (__main__.py run_pass_result ... skipping read-only passes (dry-run / reconcile-check / preview))'
scenarios: An operator runs `--mode reconcile-check`: the preflight code placed in run_pass_result is never reached, so the plan's stated skip is a no-op (harmless but the AC's claim about reconcile-check being skipped is untestable at that site).

A dry-run pass: the preflight must decide to skip BEFORE reconcile_once, but the no_write signal is only available after; if the preflight keys off target_mode it must inspect an opaque mode object the plan never characterizes.
findings.suggested_fix: State the pre-call skip predicate explicitly (e.g. skip when route == 'preview' or target_mode indicates dry-run/no-write), and either remove reconcile-check from the run_pass_result skip list or place the guard at the mode dispatch (near __main__.py:625-627) so reconcile-check is genuinely covered.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how run_pass_result distinguishes read-only passes at the wiring site — name target_mode + mode.MODE_CAPS (cap-0 => dry-run) for the mode-driven case and route=='preview' for preview — and note that reconcile-check is already short-circuited at __main__.py:626 before run_pass_result, so it need not be skipped there.
evidence: __main__.py:626-627 `if target_mode == mode_mod.Mode.RECONCILE_CHECK: return _run_reconcile_check(repo_root)` returns before run_pass() (line 634) is called

reconcile.py:238-241 shows dry-run/reconcile-check are cap-0 (`persist = mode_mod.MODE_CAPS.get(target_mode) != 0`); run_pass_result receives target_mode + route but the plan does not name which one distinguishes dry-run
run_pass (line 431) forwards target_mode/route to run_pass_result; preview reaches it via route=='preview', dry-run only via target_mode
findings.finding: The plan's read-only-skip classification at the named wiring site (run_pass_result) is imprecise about the discriminator: it lists 'dry-run / reconcile-check / preview' uniformly, but reconcile-check returns via _run_reconcile_check at __main__.py:626-627 before run_pass/run_pass_result is reached (so it never hits the wiring site), while the dry-run mode that DOES reach run_pass_result is identified only by target_mode + mode.MODE_CAPS cap-0 (persist=False), not by the `route` value — which the plan does not name.
findings.location: Approach / Sequencing — 'Wire it at the reconcile pass entry (`__main__.py` `run_pass_result` ...), skipping read-only passes (dry-run / reconcile-check / preview)'
scenarios: A dry-run pass reaches run_pass_result and the preflight must correctly identify it as read-only using target_mode/MODE_CAPS, not `route`
An implementer keys the skip on `route` alone and inadvertently runs the live preflight (building a Cloud client) on a dry-run pass, or conversely skips a live pass
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the wiring to gate on the persist/cap-0 signal: skip the preflight when `target_mode is not None and mode.MODE_CAPS.get(target_mode) == 0` (covers dry-run) and when `route == 'preview'`; drop reconcile-check from the run_pass_result skip list since it returns via _run_reconcile_check before that function is reached.

findings.finding: The plan depends on the external Jira Cloud endpoint GET /rest/api/3/project/search and asserts its response-envelope/pagination contract (values[].key, isLast, startAt) but this specific endpoint surface is used nowhere in the repo and is not verified against Jira Cloud docs — it is an asserted-but-unverified external capability.
findings.location: Approach — 'GET /rest/api/3/project/search (paginated via startAt with the response envelope's values[].key / isLast)'
scenarios: Ship the preflight; the real /project/search envelope differs (e.g. key under a nested object, or the paginated endpoint requires maxResults/expand params) → every project reads as 'invisible' → preflight FAILs FAST on a fully-correct mapping and blocks all live passes
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the Jira Cloud 'Get projects paginated' doc URL and its documented query params (startAt, maxResults) + response fields (values[].key, isLast, total) in the Approach, and add one live/recorded-fixture assertion that the parser matches the real envelope (not only the self-authored fake).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the retry-vs-fail-closed boundary (how many retries before transport-unavailable) and a pagination termination guard (handle absent/false isLast, empty values, and a max-page bound) for the project/search probe.
evidence: 'its retry helper (_retry_sleep / JQL_RETRY_COUNT)'
'A hard auth/transport error ... fails closed with its own distinct "transport unavailable" message'
pagination 'via startAt with the response envelope's values[].key / isLast' — no termination guard against a missing isLast/empty page stated
findings.finding: The plan reuses the retry helper (_retry_sleep / JQL_RETRY_COUNT) but does not state how a transient/retryable error is distinguished from a hard fail-closed transport error, nor how the paginated project/search loop terminates safely (e.g. empty values, isLast never true, or a page cap).
scenarios: A transient 5xx exhausts retries — is that transport-unavailable or does it retry forever?
project/search returns a page with isLast absent or malformed and the loop never terminates
findings.suggested_fix: Specify: retry transient errors up to JQL_RETRY_COUNT then raise transport-unavailable; loop while not isLast and values non-empty, break on a defensive max-page cap, treating a malformed envelope as transport-unavailable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that this preflight covers only the nonexistent/invisible sub-case of Problem #2 (not a 'real-but-wrong-but-visible' destination), OR strengthen the check toward create-capability / narrow the acceptance-criteria wording so the guarantee is not over-claimed.
evidence: Problem #2: 'a legacy_default pointing at a real-but-wrong (or nonexistent) project drives a mass CREATE storm into the wrong place, unguarded.'
Approach: probe checks presence 'against the standard Jira Cloud "Get projects paginated" endpoint' — visibility, not create-capability.

projects_store.py:112-130 resolve_project returns legacy_default verbatim; the write guard's allowed set = read_projects().keys() and EXCLUDES creates (per plan), so a browsable wrong legacy_default still passes both guard and this visibility preflight.
findings.finding: The preflight validates project VISIBILITY (via /rest/api/3/project/search, which reflects browse permission) as a proxy for the ability to safely receive creates. Problem failure-mode #2 explicitly names a legacy_default pointing at a 'real-but-wrong' project driving a mass CREATE storm; a real-but-wrong project the bot can browse will PASS this visibility preflight yet still misroute the CREATE storm, so the named problem is only partially solved.
findings.location: Approach — 'enumerates the bot-visible project keys'; Problem #2 'real-but-wrong (or nonexistent) project'
scenarios: legacy_default is set to a real project the bot can browse but that is the wrong destination for the legacy cohort — preflight passes, CREATE storm lands in the wrong project.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, scope the guarantee precisely: 'This preflight catches nonexistent/decommissioned/permission-lost (browse-invisible) keys. It does NOT validate that a browsable legacy_default is the CORRECT create destination — that mis-routing sub-case of Problem #2 remains out of scope and is best addressed by extending the cross-project write guard to include the resolved legacy_default.' Adjust AC wording from 'is visible' framing to match.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the exact pagination contract of /rest/api/3/project/search (offset startAt/maxResults vs token) against docs and state the loop-termination condition (isLast AND/OR exhausted offset), so the visible-project set cannot silently truncate.
evidence: acli_graph.py:78-91 — THE shared cursor walk paginates via 'nextPageToken' and terminates on 'isLast: true' OR null/absent token; startAt is not used there
The plan asserts startAt-based offset paging for /project/search — a DIFFERENT pagination model than the token walk already in the codebase
T3 EMPIRICISM: flag/field-level mismatches 'cause silent runtime failures after ship'; here a wrong terminator/offset field silently truncates the project set
findings.finding: The plan asserts /project/search paginates via startAt+isLast, but the codebase's existing Jira search pagination uses opaque nextPageToken (acli_graph.py); the plan does not reconcile which pagination model /project/search actually uses, so an unverified pagination-shape mismatch could silently truncate the visible-project set.
findings.location: Approach — 'paginated via startAt with the response envelope's values[].key / isLast'
scenarios: /project/search returns >1 page; the loop terminates early (or spins) because the assumed startAt/isLast contract does not match the live envelope → a mapped key on page 2 is judged 'not visible' → false FAIL FAST
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the pagination loop to the documented offset model (startAt += maxResults until isLast or startAt+len(values) >= total) and assert termination in the test with a two-page fixture where BAD appears only on page 2.
